implementation.engine: four Rust crates; independent length-framed application IPC and NUL-framed JSON Chromium pipes
implementation.residentRuntime: Shared five-source manifest includes codec, evaluation, pinned selector bundle, condition registry and locator wrapper; Rust, JavaScript and tests verify the same length-framed source hash.
implementation.ownership: Independent guardian owns the browser process group and profile. A group-exit barrier keeps the leader unreaped until every member stops. Shared shutdown completion never kills the guardian for slow profile cleanup; bounded operation cleanup reports guardianContinuingCleanup when necessary.
implementation.cancellation: withdraw queued allocation, consume dispatched allocation reply then dispose, close owned browser when allocation result cannot be recovered, dispose success arriving after caller deadline
implementation.cleanupMetadata: error details identify resource disposal, undispatched work or browser-shutdown fallback
implementation.navigation: Loader-aware event state retains bounded completion records. Received-event acknowledgement barriers synchronize input completion with navigation state; document commits detach the old child-frame subtree even if Chromium omits individual detach events.
implementation.locator: One isolated runtime per frame document with shared initialization and execution-time membership; ordinary locator operations retain host deadlines and retries, while opt-in assertions register exact-context resident conditions.
implementation.input: Native text and pointer input with method-specific actionability, fresh frame stability, hit interception, button/modifier cleanup and navigation barriers. Protocol results and errors carry operation input delivery progress, including replies crossing the caller deadline. Keyboard, pointer and fill/focus mutations share per-page input ownership. Key chords are validated before effects; interrupted keys are released or the affected page is closed. Pinned macOS editing commands preserve platform shortcuts. Page-level presses retain current focus and use an unbounded operation without locator navigation waiting. Undelayed clicks admit their whole bounded command sequence atomically, dispatch in wire order without reply barriers, and withdraw unsent commands on cancellation. Uncertain pointer delivery closes the owned page without replaying a release; the input lock remains held through disposal.
implementation.rendererExpiry: Wall-clock renderer guard suppresses already-expired work queued behind a blocked event loop; the Rust monotonic deadline remains authoritative.
implementation.assertions: Complete pinned predicates and bounded observations in both host-polled and opt-in resident paths. Authoritative host monotonic deadlines cannot accept late success. Responsive cancellation gathers terminal diagnostics; blocked-renderer cancellation retains bounded exact-context cleanup until acknowledgement or owner closure.
implementation.runner: Pinned flashwright-upstream-runner alias supplies scheduling and generic assertion infrastructure; _baseTest is the private boundary. Native fixtures and expect.extend browser matchers dispatch only to Flashwright. Plain library loading is independent of the scheduler. Native storageState fixtures inherit contextOptions and support explicit object and file overrides.
implementation.handshake: The client requires every implemented operation capability before dispatching browser allocation; missing keyboard.press is covered by a rejecting fake-driver test.
implementation.evaluationErrors: Explicit execution/argument-decoding/result-serialization stages with private codec error identity and independently bounded UTF-16 diagnostics; Node argument encoding uses the same classification.
implementation.launchPolicy: Default CDP Chromium arguments extracted from the pinned reference, including default headed/headless variants; the guardian substitutes its owned profile at the retained position. Shared benchmark contracts compare actual emitted launch arguments.
implementation.pageFocusPolicy: Main page sessions enable Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled, matching pinned Playwright initialization. Two-page visibility/focus and fresh pointer-frame checks conform; a blocked handler in one page leaves another page usable.
implementation.testFailureCleanup: Unittest cleanup registered immediately after owner creation; only the worker/driver is terminated, and guardian completion is awaited before diagnostic streams close. Four intentionally failed setup/body cases cover both owner paths.
implementation.protocolAttribution: Opt-in external byte-preserving Chromium pipe proxy records bounded command metadata and script hashes without argument/result payloads. Two clock calibrations bound Node/Python epoch offset, and an independent verifier recomputes correlated phase accounting. Instrumented timing is diagnostic only.
implementation.residentRegistryExperiment: Default-off fair registry with synchronous selector sharing, coalesced fallback timers and indexed CSS lookup. The preceding evaluation-helper checkpoint records 104 core groups, Node22 and 57 registry cases pass with private evaluation helpers. The two residency-on Playwright comparisons show about 5.0% and 5.7% less complete-run time, below the 10% material target, with failure-path median regressions. The preceding sustained-load matrix applies to its recorded binary only. See compatibility/evidence/evaluation-helper-performance-checkpoint-2026-10-08.json
implementation.ordinaryResourceClose: Ordinary page/context closure waits for its actual Chromium acknowledgement. The bounded operation-cancellation disposal budget no longer causes a slow ordinary close to shut down the entire browser. Unit test withholds close acknowledgement for 750ms; full emulated Linux suite passes.
implementation.benchmarkBrowserBinding: Core reports bind exact browser path, SHA-256, version and distribution; new benchmark admission and independent verification require that identity. compatibility/evidence/browser-distribution-checkpoint-2026-10-07.json
implementation.runtimeSourceEncoding: Resident source files remain ASCII, enforced by the Rust build. Unicode runtime values use JavaScript escapes without changing diagnostics or supported application text. A literal U+2026 caused a verified installation regression; compatibility/evidence/ascii-runtime-checkpoint-2026-10-07.json
implementation.residentResourceMeasurement: Fixed-work sustained-load harness covers quiet text, property-only and mutation workloads at 1/32/128 conditions with all six engine orders, actual launch flags, backend/application counts, source/browser/binary binding and self-contained verification logs. Corrected CPU accounting survives macOS zombie resets. compatibility/evidence/resident-load-checkpoint-2026-10-08.json
implementation.evaluationRuntime: Private helper code is installed once per main-world unique identity and shared by concurrent callers. Setup belongs to the document and survives caller cancellation without running user callbacks. Each invocation gets a fresh value codec. Calls remain concurrent and are never replayed across navigation. See compatibility/evidence/evaluation-helper-checkpoint-2026-10-08.json All 64 ordinary and four instrumented launches independently verify. Protocol accounting records six helper installations and 81 callbacks per launch; each callback wrapper has 107 UTF-16 units. Default-mode complete runs remain near parity with Playwright; residency-on runs use about 5.0–5.7% less time. See compatibility/evidence/evaluation-helper-performance-checkpoint-2026-10-08.json These performance results predate cookie/storage-state implementation and apply to the recorded binary only.
implementation.contextStorage: Context-owned visited origins survive page closure. Native context-scoped cookie commands serialize with state snapshots. Private origin pages fulfill their requests locally, bypass service workers and preserve exact UTF-16 entries. Cancelled prior-document interceptions are consumed without replay; unrelated fulfillment failures propagate. Initial restoration finishes before publication, snapshot files replace atomically, and uncertain mutation acknowledgements retire the affected context without replay. SPECS S4.j records the intentional reference service-worker difference. See compatibility/evidence/storage-checkpoint-2026-10-08.json
implementation.externalWatchdog: Owned process identities are terminated from parents to descendants, with a two-second grace at each stage, ten seconds for staged cleanup and two seconds for final forced escalation. Zombie owners retain the initial descendant grace. Resource reports record the policy, signals and remaining observations; unresolved cleanup returns a nonzero status. Ten Python tests and six real Chromium shutdown cases pass on native macOS and emulated Linux. See compatibility/evidence/watchdog-cleanup-2026-10-08/report.json
implementation.outboundLimits: Driver replies are validated and encoded once before writing. Byte/depth/node overflow becomes a per-call ResourceLimitError, retaining input delivery and cleanup without replay. UTF-16 errors and diagnostics share the payload node budget; fixed error metadata stays representable. Events that cannot fit send a global error and close. Allocations remain private until their reply is accepted; rejection performs bounded disposal. See compatibility/evidence/output-limits-checkpoint-2026-10-08.json
implementation.binaryAttachments: Protocol 5 keeps request-scoped raw/base64 application streams, 32 MiB decoded attachments, two active reservations and 64 KiB chunks. The Chromium JSON reader now admits typed response bodies beyond the ordinary 8 MiB reply/event cap. Its hard wire bound accounts for worst-case JSON escaping; it releases large frame buffers after use and ignores cancelled reply values. Complete oversized ordinary replies reject only their call. Fatal event/wire failures preserve their original error through page/context cleanup. Chromium JSON frames are still buffered, so this is not a constant-memory streaming CDP decoder. See compatibility/evidence/browser-payload-checkpoint-2026-10-08.json
implementation.lifecycleVerification: The deadline fixture now gives each of its nine independent scenarios the original ten-second subprocess bound. Each discovered lifecycle module has its own 240-second watchdog; output-limit, binary and watchdog modules retain their 180-second limits. Public operation deadlines and assertions are unchanged. All 58 counted lifecycle cases pass on native macOS and emulated Linux, nine focused scenarios pass on Node22, and the complete emulated Linux core passes all 27 groups. The native/Linux production binaries are unchanged from the binary-attachment checkpoint. Historical failures remain retained; native Linux and performance/release gates remain open. See compatibility/evidence/lifecycle-budget-checkpoint-2026-10-08.json
implementation.browserPayloadVerification: At 179 matching source hashes, all 27 native macOS core groups and all 27 emulated Linux core groups pass, including 61 lifecycle cases per platform, with four focused Node22/headless-shell groups. Real-browser tests preserve a 9 MiB all-byte binary body and 2 MiB NUL text with a JSON representation above 12 MiB. Public response-body differentials match pinned Playwright byte-for-byte with one HTTP request per body. The initial Linux launch failed before creating a container because its local image was missing; rebuilding the pinned recipe restored the environment, and a separately recorded run passed. No new performance claim; native Linux and release gates remain open. See compatibility/evidence/browser-payload-checkpoint-2026-10-08.json
implementation.screenshots: Page-owned serialization and caller deadlines retain preparation through cancellation. Opaque browser object identities restore only the original prepared documents; read-only geometry follows navigation. Typed screenshot replies obey the negotiated attachment bound and pixel dimensions are checked before browser capture. Unknown restoration state retires the affected page without replacing the original error. Native page-window bounds and emulated screen metrics follow the pinned reference. SPECS S4.k records the intentional suppression of expired queued preparation. Even an unmodified out-of-process capture retains the reference child-renderer evaluation dependency through temporary owned sessions. Late successful attachment replies are recovered for cleanup; a blocked renderer times out while its parent remains usable. Exact pixel fixtures establish rendering readiness because both engines can capture before an iframe first composites.
implementation.screenshotsVerification: All 29 native macOS core groups and all 29 emulated Linux core groups pass, including 57 Rust tests and 64 lifecycle cases per platform. Six focused Node22/headless-shell groups also pass. All 187 final source hashes match across this matrix. Child/parent rendering readiness makes image comparison independent of first-paint races shared by both engines. A blocked remote renderer times out and releases its temporary session without losing the parent. Screenshot differentials compare decoded pixels and dimensions, including navigation during fonts, natural viewport, unmodified cross-process frames and a 12.6 MB PNG. Per-page deadlines, exact preparation restoration, atomic files, payload limits and cancellation pass. Native window/screen metrics now match the pinned reference. No new performance claim; prior timings apply only to their recorded binaries. See compatibility/evidence/screenshots-checkpoint-2026-10-08.json
implementation.pageErrors: Native Error name/message/stack follow pinned Chromium formatting. Original event JSON preserves exact UTF-16 through bounded Rust/Node framing; no renderer callback or retained history is added. Exceptions are routed only to live published pages by browser/session identity. Shared waits remain independent of pending evaluations and remove their listeners on settlement. Workers, out-of-process frames, context error events and pageErrors history remain outside this slice.
implementation.pageErrorVerification: All 31 native macOS core groups pass, including 58 Rust tests and 65 lifecycle cases. Seven focused Node22/headless-shell groups and ten focused Linux amd64-emulation groups pass at the same 191 source hashes. The final three diagnostic differentials match all 20 error cases and nine lifecycle checks exactly against Playwright 1.60.0. Packed ESM/CommonJS consumers preserve Error inference, and oversized exceptions fail with ResourceLimitError and release owned resources. This is functional evidence only; a full current Linux core and native Linux/performance/release gates remain open. See compatibility/evidence/diagnostics-checkpoint-2026-10-08.json

No complete runner adapter, aliases, pnpm or Yarn verification yet
Value coverage is a tested development subset, not full differential conformance with every Playwright evaluation case
Emulated Linux functional evidence does not satisfy native Linux performance gates
Navigation/network support is the tested development subset; URLPattern, full header/cookie variants, routing, API requests and service-worker semantics require further conformance
Screenshot masks, element capture, assertions and runner artifact policies remain unimplemented; persistent Page.keyboard down/up, sequential typing and broader keyboard APIs remain unimplemented
Cross-process child-frame routing explicitly rejects; FrameLocator, handles and broader frame/navigation conformance remain unfinished
Native text input containing unpaired UTF-16 surrogates rejects explicitly; selector and read strings preserve those units
Locator coverage is an experimental tested subset; complete option/export enforcement and adversarial input/cancellation conformance remain release gates
Popup/dialog/console coverage remains unfinished; pageerror supports the main-page session and same-process child frames, with worker/out-of-process/context events and retained history still open
TodoMVC migration verification uses the public demo URL retained by the original fixture; asset hashes are checked before and after but offline application reproduction is not yet available

Resident assertions remain opt-in. The preceding evaluation-helper 64-launch ordinary plan and four-launch protocol attribution are complete and independently verified. Default-mode complete time is near parity; residency-on runs are about 5.0–5.7% faster, below the material target. Failure-path and observed-maximum regressions remain. Native Linux, contention, remaining APIs, platform packages and release gates are open.

Basic storage excludes IndexedDB, existing-context setStorageState, non-HTTP origins and out-of-process child-frame collection. Snapshot origin, UTF-16 and serialized-message caps fail explicitly. Temporary pages bypass service-worker interception; the pinned reference can execute worker-supplied application code during fallback collection, an intentional documented difference rather than full service-worker parity.

Cookie/storage-state conformance adds 81 core groups over three native macOS configurations, focused Node22 checks, and three complete storage-corpus runs on emulated Linux. The full Linux run after the interception fix exceeded its lifecycle watchdog budget and remains incomplete; its forced cleanup left an owned profile in the stopped container, which was removed. The subsequent watchdog checkpoint repairs orderly profile cleanup; the full Linux verification gap remains open. Ordinary performance has not been rerun for this new binary; prior timing and CPU claims remain bound to their immutable checkpoints.

The watchdog checkpoint retains native and emulated Linux full lifecycle batches that exceeded their unchanged 240-second job budget under shared-host activity. Both forced shutdowns left no owned process/profile. All three suspect recovery cases passed separately on both platforms; those checks do not replace a full matrix pass.

Output-limit conformance passes 54 native core groups, eight Node22 groups and 26 focused emulated Linux cases at 170 matching source hashes. A Linux Rust compilation exceeded its 120-second job budget; after build preparation the full lifecycle batch exceeded its unchanged 240-second budget following a blocked-pointer case failure. The complete public lifecycle class then passed separately. Both failed runs are retained, with no observed process/profile residue; the full Linux matrix remains incomplete. No ordinary performance result applies to this new binary yet.

Binary-attachment conformance passes 27 native core groups including 50 lifecycle cases, four focused Node22 groups plus five headless-shell binary cases, and 31 focused emulated Linux browser cases at 178 matching source hashes. The broad Linux lifecycle run exceeded its unchanged 240-second budget. Its nine-client deadline fixture also exceeded a 10-second aggregate allowance; a diagnostic rerun completed all nine cleanly in 13.847 seconds. The broad failure remains retained, and fixture budgeting/full Linux verification remain open. No new performance claim.

The lifecycle-budget checkpoint completes the current full functional matrix under Linux amd64 emulation. Earlier incomplete runs remain historical failures, including an older blocked-pointer failure whose traceback was lost before immediate diagnostic reporting existed. The known aggregate fixture budget faults are repaired; this does not retrospectively establish the cause of every older failure. Native Linux and broader contention acceptance remain open. See compatibility/evidence/lifecycle-budget-checkpoint-2026-10-08.json

Screenshot preparation in out-of-process frames is not implemented; only unmodified capture is supported there. Images are limited to 32767 pixels on each axis, 16777216 total pixels and the negotiated encoded attachment bound (32 MiB by default). Screenshot cleanup has an independent bounded budget and can retire a page when restoration is uncertain. Native viewport setup changed in this implementation, so previous timing observations do not apply to this binary.
